notes: The Bay Area Reporter, San Francisco's gay community newspaper, 1 April 1971 to 24 December 1975: the 121 issues of those years in the Internet Archive collection bayareareporter (GLBT Historical Society scans, identifiers BAR_YYYYMMDD). The items have no hOCR; text and leaves are rebuilt from each item's _djvu.xml (/mnt/project-files/bar/dl_djvu.py), and citations give the issue date and the zero-based leaf. Read by hand, with no reader pass: the numbered-address passages that survive the advertisement filter, clustered by address (cluster_bar.py), and a pass over event words (fire, arson, grand opening, moved, closed) for the places the paper names without a number. extra.candidate is the row key in /mnt/project-files/bar/decisions_bar1.py. Kept: openings, moves and closings of bars, clubs, restaurants, shops, theaters and baths as businesses; fires; and the community's institutions at an address (the Society for Individual Rights center, the Metropolitan Community Church, the Golden Gate Gay Liberation House, the National Transsexual Counseling Unit, the Alice B. Toklas club, the Helping Hands center). Not kept: anyone named as an owner, manager, bartender, performer or patron; arrests and raids, which the paper reports by the names of those arrested; personal and classified advertisements; bare weekly advertising; meeting places; out-of-town copy. A bar is named as a business and never by its owner. The paper is mostly advertising and most openings are known only from a display advertisement, whose bar name the OCR often garbles: extra.placement_note says where a name or number came from when the cited passage does not print it cleanly, always another issue of the same paper. extra.number_as_printed keeps a printed number that another issue corrects. The paper is copyright BAR Media, Inc.; raw.text is a clause only and no text is committed.

coverage.remaining: 1976 to 2005 remain: 1,393 issues in the collection, 8 January 1976 to 28 July 2005.
coverage.note: 121 issues; 4,702 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, 2,955 windows before the advertisement filter and 555 after it, in 466 address clusters, plus 149 event-word passages, all read by hand. 75 findings written, each quote found again in the issue's text. 54 resolved and published on 45 pages (3 seeded: 1710 Golden Gate Avenue, 3221 Mission Street and 758 Haight Street, a condominium building seeded with its 5 unit pages); 7 of them placed by hand on a parcel whose range holds a number EAS does not. 21 unresolved: 5 thin single facts held on parcels with no page (extra.placed_apn), and 16 where the building is gone or the number falls between two parcels, each with its reason in resolution.note. The held Bernal Journal fact on 3223 Mission Street (bernal-journals-0042) was taken up with the page this batch seeded there.
